title: Legend foldout with semantic batching and screen-reader breadcrumb
creator: Avery Park
description: Create a new pattern for series legends that scales to long lists without bloating the DOM or degrading assistive technology experience. The pattern is an initially compact summary bar with a progressive foldout that loads interactive legend rows on demand using semantic batching and a screen-reader breadcrumb summary. Aim: maintain keyboard-first navigation, clear ARIA semantics, and sub-50ms interaction latency on mid-tier devices while keeping markup and repaint cost minimal.
acceptance_criteria: Compact summary shows up to 6 series names and an aggregate "available series" count when >6
Foldout opens with keyboard (Enter/Space) and arrow navigation; focus lands on first interactive row
Screen-reader users hear a single concise summary on render and an updated breadcrumb when the foldout opens
Legend DOM nodes are virtualized: initial DOM nodes <= 12 for lists of up to 10,000 series
Micro-icons for series rendered as a single shared canvas sprite to avoid per-row SVG DOM cost
Engineering benchmarks demonstrate <50ms main-thread spike when opening a foldout with 500 visible rows on a Chrome mid-tier device
design_decisions: Use listbox + option semantics for interactive legend rows (role=listbox, role=option) to work with screen readers and keyboard navigation
Provide a semantic, aria-live region containing a one-line breadcrumb summary (e.g., '3 of 182 series visible; press enter to expand') instead of attempting to call out every series on mount
Implement progressive hydration: initially render static li elements with role=button appearance; replace with full interactive rows only when the foldout is expanded or when row is focused
Group series visually by data family (e.g., metrics, predictions) and expose optional collapse groups to reduce cognitive load
Render color swatches and small plotlets using an offscreen canvas sprite sheet and CSS background positioning to avoid per-row SVG nodes
Threshold for auto-condense: when series_count > 8, switch to condensed summary + foldout pattern; make this configurable via token (legend.condense-threshold)
Use CSS custom properties for spacing, tokenized color contrast, and focus outline so platform themes can override without reworking DOM structure
tech_risks: Screen reader behavior differs across NVDA/JAWS/VoiceOver; aria-live summary may be suppressed in some contexts
Virtualization/hydration introduces focus management edge cases when keyboard users rapidly traverse rows
Canvas sprite technique may complicate color token overrides for user themes and requires a clear mapping between token names and sprite frames
Perf regression on older browsers when using requestIdleCallback polyfills; need a robust fallback path
tasks: Create Figma exploration file and token mapping (DES-901234-figma)
Prototype a static HTML/CSS/JS demo to validate keyboard and screen-reader flows
Run an engineering spike to measure main-thread costs for hydration strategies (ENG spike ticket TBD)
Accessibility review session with UX researcher and a11y engineer
Implement design tokens for legend.condense-threshold, legend-row-height, legend-swatch-size
Add unit and integration tests for keyboard navigation and aria announcements
Document pattern in component library guidelines and add migration notes for existing charts
comments: 2026-03-01 Avery Park: Initial ticket created after UX spike. Goal is to solve both DOM bloat and a11y verbosity for large series sets.
2026-03-03 Sofia Alvarez: Pushed first Figma frames focusing on the summary bar and condensed row states. Linked above. Please review color token mappings.
2026-03-05 Rohit Menon (Engineering): Requested clarification on animation timing and hydration triggers. Suggested using focus/keyboard open to eagerly hydrate for a better keyboard experience.

2026-03-07 Accessibility review: Recommend moving from aria-live polite to a single advisory role=status announce when foldout first appears; also flag potential VoiceOver suppression when the list is rendered programmatically.

2026-03-09 Ben Clarke (Performance): Ran a quick spike. Hydrating 500 rows with naive DOM construction produced a 220ms main-thread spike. Prototype using batched requestAnimationFrame hydration reduced that to 38ms on Pixel 3A. Recommend batching + idle callbacks.
2026-03-11 Sofia Alvarez: Updated acceptance criteria to require <50ms spike and added token for condense threshold. Removed annotation controls from scope to keep initial iteration focused.
2026-03-12 PM feedback: Prioritize keyboard-first flow and ensure condensed mode is toggleable via API for customers who prefer full legend by default.
